sources.title: Report of the OECD/NEA-Vattenfall T-Junction Benchmark exercise
A CFD benchmarking exercise based on flow mixing in a T-junction

sources.note: Experimental data are owned by Vattenfall R&D. Obtain and redistribute tabular datasets only under the applicable permission and attribution terms.

geometry.coordinate_system: Cartesian right-handed; main pipe axis +X; branch inlet axis +Z; origin at centreline intersection
geometry.fluid_domain_definition: Boolean union of the main-pipe and branch-pipe cylindrical bores; the solid test-block exterior is not part of the fluid domain

branch_inlet.measurement_plane_note: Distance is positive upstream along the +Z branch axis; the benchmark report uses its own signed coordinate convention.

inlet_profile_notes: The main-pipe inlet profile is fully developed and was measured at x=-3D_main.
The branch-pipe inlet profile is developing because the available upstream length is about 20 diameters.
The benchmark inlet velocity profiles were measured in an earlier test at main/branch flow-rate ratio 2; branch flow stayed at 6 L/s and the main flow was changed to 9 L/s for the benchmark.
The benchmark report requires careful inlet-profile definition; uniform velocity is a smoke-test simplification, not the benchmark boundary condition.
operating_conditions.property_reference: Use water properties from the 1967 ASME Steam Tables as specified by the benchmark report, with thermal-expansion data referenced to Incropera and DeWitt. Record the selected interpolation state and property values in every future physical-validation run.

inlet_velocity_profiles.availability: described and plotted in report; tabular files were distributed to benchmark participants

reference_measurements.data_status: Reference locations and quantities are recorded; original Vattenfall tabular files are not bundled until redistribution permission and source files are confirmed.

comparisons: downstream PIV mean and RMS velocity
future_validation_plan.numerical_methods: Select and document turbulence/thermal model, temporal resolution, wall treatment and averaging duration before claiming benchmark validation.
future_validation_plan.smoke_test_warning: A two-step or otherwise short CFD smoke run verifies only runtime handoff and process completion. It cannot establish convergence, turbulence statistics, thermal mixing accuracy or agreement with experimental measurements.
